correctness.rationale: At the actual seven-entry frozen record tree (six files and the verification subtree), I read the complete RESULT proof and original checker. Duplicate demands cannot win under envy; unique satisfied r-sets are disjoint. Any packing is realized with k r-bundles and m-rk singleton leftovers because n-k>=m-rk, for n>=m and r>=2. This proves W=nu(H), including all nontrivial boundary cases. The polynomial r=2 case and NP-hard fixed r>=3 padding are correct. Independent fresh literal enumeration (not executing the uploaded checker) matched W and packing on 1661 demand profiles, and separately verified singleton occupancy p0 and means for (M,n)=(3,3),(3,4),(4,4),(6,5). The fixed-j factorial moments converge to e^(-jt), while E intersecting singleton pairs is exactly M/2*(M-1-C(m-r,r))*n(n-1)/M^2*(1-2/M)^(n-2)=O_r(1/m); hence total variation and expectation difference vanish. First/second moments settle one-sided windows. Infinite claims rest on these analytic arguments, not finite checks.

originality.rationale: The full original claim overcredited the deterministic identity and classical coupon-collector threshold. Fiat-Wingarten (2009) Observation 5 at price zero gives the single-minded winner/loser restriction; with singleton parking it implies W=nu(H), and graph/set packing algorithms are classical. Erdős-Rényi and Newman-Shepp cover the two-coupon window. The narrowed claim is a quantitative O_r(1/m) coupling of optimal complete envy-free welfare with the singleton occupancy count for uniformly sampled overlapping r-sets, with full welfare Poisson distribution and mean. Neither the checked pricing nor coupon-collector source alone states that welfare comparison; broad Resultary search found no earlier direct same theorem (self-hit excluded). Best-of-knowledge PASS qualified by unindexed hypergraph results and inaccessible full 2026 Leontief paper.

value.rationale: The maximum welfare under complete envy-free perfect-complement allocations is a mathematically natural stochastic optimization invariant. The precise Poisson law, sharp crowd-out window, exact zero-welfare formula and a finite explicit O_r(1/m) error relative to singleton occupancy make the optimal fair outcome quantitatively decidable, not just a simulation or a repackaged raw occupancy count. The contribution is narrow and the methods are classical; no general coupon-collector, auction or complexity novelty is claimed.

final_claim: At fixed r>=2 for n>=m i.i.d. uniform r-set requests, the optimal complete envy-free welfare W has Poisson(e^-t) distributional limit and convergent mean when n/M-log M-loglog M ->t. A finite explicit bound dTV(L(W),L(S))<=E C=O_r(1/m) compares W with the number S of singleton request types; exact zero-welfare event/formula and one-sided thresholds also hold. The known zero-price single-minded winner restriction, packing identity and coupon collector window are explicitly credited as earlier mathematics.
